Section 1

New patient forms

Please complete these before your first visit. Bringing them filled out saves about 15 minutes at check-in. If you'd rather complete them in the office, plan to arrive 30 minutes early instead of 15.

Patient Registration PDF · 2 pages · Demographics, emergency contact Medical History Questionnaire PDF · 4 pages · Conditions, medications, allergies, family history HIPAA Acknowledgment PDF · 2 pages · Notice of Privacy Practices acknowledgment Insurance Verification PDF · 1 page · Insurance and subscriber information Photo Release for Clinical Documentation PDF · 1 page · Optional — for tracking moles, lesions, treatment response Authorization to Release Records PDF · 1 page · If transferring records from a prior dermatologist

All forms can also be completed digitally through the patient portal once your portal account is activated (we email the activation link the business day after your appointment is scheduled).

Section 2

What to bring to your first appointment

The more of this you can bring, the more we can accomplish in our first visit together.

  • Government-issued photo ID
  • Current insurance card (front and back)
  • Completed new patient forms (or arrive 30 min early)
  • Referral from your primary care provider if your insurance requires one
  • Complete list of current medications including dosages
  • List of supplements, vitamins, and herbal products
  • Names and dates of recent topical products you've tried
  • Any prior dermatology records, biopsy reports, or photos
  • List of allergies (medications, latex, adhesives, anesthetics)
  • Names of other physicians involved in your care
  • Form of payment for copay (we accept cash, check, all major credit cards, Care Credit, FSA/HSA cards)
  • For minor patients: parent or legal guardian must accompany

For skin exams and rash visits: please come without makeup on the areas of concern, with hair pulled back if scalp evaluation is needed, and prepared to change into a gown. For nail concerns, please remove polish before the visit.

Section 3

Insurance plans accepted

We are in-network with most major commercial plans serving the Pacific Northwest. Please call your insurance carrier to confirm specialist coverage — networks change without notice and we cannot guarantee in-network status for any specific plan.

  • BCBS of Oregon (PPO & HMO)
  • Regence BlueShield
  • Aetna (commercial & Medicare Advantage)
  • Cigna (most plans)
  • UnitedHealthcare (commercial)
  • UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage
  • Pacific Source Health Plans
  • Providence Health Plan
  • Kaiser Permanente PPO (Added Choice)
  • Moda Health
  • HealthNet
  • Medicare (Original)
  • Medicare Advantage (most local plans)
  • Oregon Health Plan (OHP/Medicaid) — limited slots
  • TriWest / TRICARE (most regions)
  • Samaritan Health Plans
  • Trillium Community Health Plan
  • VA Community Care referrals

A note about HMO and EPO plans

Most HMO and many EPO plans require a referral from your primary care provider before they will cover a specialty dermatology visit. Without a valid referral on file, your insurance may deny the claim and you would be responsible for the full cost of the visit. Please confirm with your insurance whether a referral is required and have your PCP send it to us before your appointment.

Fax for referrals (503) 555-1872

If we are out-of-network with your plan, you are welcome to be seen as a self-pay patient or under out-of-network benefits if your plan offers them. Our office can provide a Good Faith Estimate of charges before your visit per the No Surprises Act.

Section 4

Billing & payment

We bill your insurance directly for in-network covered services. Copays are due at time of service. Coinsurance and deductible balances are billed after we receive the explanation of benefits (EOB) from your insurance.

Payment methods accepted

  • Cash, personal check, and money order
  • All major credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover)
  • Debit cards
  • HSA and FSA cards
  • Care Credit (medical financing — applications accepted at front desk)
  • Online payment through patient portal

Pay your bill online

Sign in to patient portal to pay

Financial hardship policy

We understand that medical bills can be a serious burden. If you are unable to pay your balance in full, please contact our billing office at (503) 555-1873 as soon as possible — we offer payment plans, can sometimes apply a financial hardship discount based on income and family size, and can assist you with applying for Care Credit or other financing. Our goal is to keep you in care; the worst thing you can do is avoid the conversation.

Cosmetic services

Cosmetic services are self-pay and payment is due at time of service. We provide a written estimate during your consultation. We do not accept insurance for any cosmetic procedure. Care Credit is widely used for cosmetic visits.

Billing questions

For questions about a bill you've received, the EOB from your insurance, or financial assistance, call our billing office directly:

(503) 555-1873 · Monday–Thursday 9 a.m. – 4 p.m.

Section 5

Patient portal

Our patient portal lets you securely message your provider, view test and biopsy results, request prescription refills, complete forms ahead of your visit, view past visit summaries, and pay bills online.

Sign in or activate your account

If you've been a patient and have not received your activation email, call our front desk and we'll resend it. Activation links expire after 7 days for security.

Sign in to portal Activate new account Forgot password?

The patient portal is encrypted in transit and at rest, and is the secure way to share clinical information with our team. Do not use email for protected health information — email is not encrypted and should not be used for sharing medical details, photos of concerning lesions, or insurance information.

Section 6

Telehealth visits

We offer secure video visits for appropriate concerns. Telehealth works particularly well for medication management follow-ups, established acne patients, isotretinoin monthly visits, post-procedure check-ins, and some new rashes that can be evaluated visually with good lighting.

What telehealth works well for

  • Acne medication follow-up and adjustment
  • Eczema flare management for established patients
  • Isotretinoin monthly check-ins
  • Post-procedure wound checks
  • Medication side-effect discussions
  • Many psoriasis follow-ups
  • Questions about test results

What requires an in-person visit

  • Initial skin examinations and mole evaluations
  • Anything that may need a biopsy
  • Procedures of any kind
  • Concerning new lesions that need dermatoscopy
  • Hair loss evaluations
  • Most pediatric first visits

How to prepare

  • Use a device with a working camera and microphone — phone, tablet, or computer all work
  • Find a private, well-lit room (natural light from a window is ideal)
  • Make sure your internet connection is stable
  • Have a list of current medications ready
  • If the visit is about a specific skin concern, plan how you'll position the camera or use a second device to show it clearly
  • Test the connection by signing into the portal before your visit time

Telehealth visits are billed the same as in-person visits and are covered by most insurance plans. You'll receive an Estimate of Charges at scheduling. If we determine during the telehealth visit that you really need to be seen in person, we'll convert the visit (no additional charge) and schedule the in-person follow-up.

Section 7

Prescription refills

The fastest way to request a refill is through the patient portal — those messages route directly to our nursing team and are processed within one business day.

How to request a refill

  • Preferred: Patient portal message to "Nursing / Refills"
  • Ask your pharmacy to send an electronic refill request — these route to us automatically
  • Call our refill line at (503) 555-1870 and select the refill option from the menu

Please allow one full business day for refill processing. Refills requested on Friday afternoons or weekends will be processed the next business day. If you're going to run out, request a few days ahead.

Controlled substances and isotretinoin

Isotretinoin and certain other monitored medications cannot be refilled without a current visit on file. iPLEDGE-regulated isotretinoin requires monthly visits and electronic prescriptions per federal regulation.

If you haven't been seen in over a year

For most chronic prescriptions, we require an annual visit before refilling. If you're due, please request an appointment alongside your refill request and we'll do our best to get you in before you run out.

Section 8

Lab & pathology results

Biopsy results typically return within 5–7 business days. Lab work returns sooner — most within 1–3 business days. All results post to the patient portal automatically as they come back.

How we communicate results

  • Routine, reassuring results — posted to the portal with a brief explanation from your provider
  • Results requiring follow-up — your provider or nurse will call you directly, and the result posts to the portal afterward
  • Cancer diagnoses — always communicated by phone before posting; we schedule a follow-up visit at the same call
  • Results you want explained — message your provider through the portal anytime; we'll respond within 2 business days

If you haven't heard about a result after 10 business days, please call us — pathology occasionally delays, and we'd rather hear from you than have anything fall through.

Section 9

HIPAA & privacy

Your medical information is protected under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and applicable Oregon state law. Our complete Notice of Privacy Practices is available at the front desk and as a PDF below.

In short:

  • We use your information to provide care, run our practice, and bill for services
  • We do not sell your information to anyone
  • We share information with other providers involved in your care, with your insurance, and with public health authorities when legally required
  • We share with family members or designated representatives only with your written authorization
  • You have the right to access, copy, and correct your medical record
  • You have the right to request an accounting of disclosures
  • You have the right to file a complaint without retaliation

Full Notice of Privacy Practices PDF · 8 pages

For privacy concerns or to file a HIPAA complaint, contact our Privacy Officer at (503) 555-1875 or write to: Privacy Officer, Westgate Family Dermatology, 2814 Westgate Boulevard, Suite 200, Beaverton, OR 97005.

Section 10

Patient rights & responsibilities

You have the right to

  • Be treated with respect and dignity by every member of our staff
  • Receive care without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, or disability
  • A clear explanation of your diagnosis, treatment plan, and reasonable alternatives in language you understand
  • Refuse any treatment and to be told what may happen if you do
  • Have your questions answered honestly, including questions about cost
  • Have an interpreter at no charge if needed
  • Bring a friend, family member, or advocate to any appointment
  • Privacy during examinations and treatments
  • Confidentiality of your medical information
  • A copy of your medical record at reasonable cost
  • Voice concerns or complaints without fear of retaliation
  • A second opinion from another qualified provider

You are asked to

  • Give us accurate, complete information about your health history, medications, and concerns
  • Ask questions when something isn't clear
  • Follow the agreed-upon treatment plan, or tell us if you can't
  • Keep your appointments, or cancel/reschedule with at least 24 hours' notice when possible
  • Arrive 15 minutes early to allow time for check-in
  • Pay for services as agreed, or contact our billing office if you can't
  • Treat our staff and other patients with respect

Late cancellation & no-show policy

We charge a $50 fee for cancellations with less than 24 hours' notice and for no-shows. We waive the fee for genuine emergencies and illness, but ask that you call us as early as possible. Repeated no-shows may affect ability to schedule future appointments.

Section 11

Non-discrimination & accessibility

Westgate Family Dermatology complies with applicable Federal civil rights laws and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, disability, sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation. We do not exclude people or treat them differently because of these characteristics.

We provide free aids and services to people with disabilities to communicate effectively with us, including qualified sign language interpreters and written information in alternative formats (large print, audio, accessible electronic formats).

We provide free language services to people whose primary language is not English, including qualified interpreters and information written in other languages. To request these services, call (503) 555-1870.

If you believe we have failed to provide these services or discriminated in any way, you can file a grievance with our Civil Rights Coordinator at (503) 555-1875. You can also file a civil rights complaint with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights.

Have a question we didn't cover?

Our front desk handles dozens of questions a day. There's a very good chance they've already answered yours. Call (503) 555-1870 or message us through the patient portal.
